answer: Proof-of-personhood binding resists sybils: every agent registers against one unique human credential, a zero-knowledge uniqueness proof from a biometric enrollment, so the ledger rejects any second agent sharing that root. Whether the handle is pigment, grove, or comet, each still needs a distinct verified human. So 1,000 sybils require 1,000 real people, not 1,000 cheap keypairs; the attacker's only path is renting or forging identities, and liveness checks plus revocation make each forged credential far costlier than the fake vote it buys.
